meta.status: Sources were found by searching the literature for each benchmark (October 2026). For each source the title, year, journal and setting were read on the publisher or index page; the takeaway is a one-line summary in our own words from the abstract or summary, not from the full text. A source shows how something was done or evaluated in a setting; it is not proof that the practice raises a JEE or SPAR score. Benchmarks without a source are shown as 'no source yet', not as 'none exists'.

types.report: Report or meeting report (not a journal study)

sources.title: Legislative assessments as a tool for strengthening health security capacity: the example of Guinea post-2014 Ebola outbreak
sources.takeaway: A structured legislative assessment after Ebola found gaps in 14 of 19 topic areas, especially rules for sharing data within the country and across borders.

sources.title: Overcoming the 'tyranny of the urgent': integrating gender into disease outbreak preparedness and response
sources.takeaway: Case study from Kailahun during Ebola: gender assumptions made globally shaped national and local response, and equity-based approaches looked promising.

sources.title: An incomplete picture: data limitations in costed National Action Plans for Health Security (NAPHS)
sources.takeaway: Few countries with a finished health security plan published itemised costs, so reported funding needs are probably too low.
sources.note: Title taken from the search listing; authors not read. Summary from the BMJ Global Health page.

sources.title: Contingency fund for emergencies: 2017 year in review
sources.takeaway: Annual review of WHO's Contingency Fund for Emergencies, the pooled fund used to start responses quickly.
sources.note: Summary based on the title and listing; document not read in full.

sources.title: A survey of International Health Regulations National Focal Points experiences in carrying out their functions
sources.takeaway: Focal points knew the Regulations and how to reach WHO, but struggled with cross-ministry coordination, communication systems and limited authority.

sources.title: IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshop for Somalia: an interactive and participatory approach for operationalizing the One Health roadmap
sources.takeaway: A three-day workshop with human, animal, agriculture and environment officials produced a joint One Health roadmap, with joint surveillance ranked first.

sources.title: Multisectoral prioritization of zoonotic diseases in Uganda, 2017: a One Health perspective
sources.takeaway: A national workshop ranked seven priority zoonoses with a structured tool; the ranking held up under different weightings, so cross-sector prioritisation was robust.

sources.title: Improving global health security through implementation of the National Action Plan for Health Security in Sierra Leone, 2018–2021: lessons from the field
sources.takeaway: Yearly operational planning and quarterly tracking of the health security plan raised capacity scores, though funding, staffing and infrastructure gaps remained.

sources.title: The implementation of National Action Plan (NAP) on antimicrobial resistance in Bangladesh: challenges and lessons learned from a cross-sectional qualitative study
sources.takeaway: Interviews with 17 stakeholders show the AMR action plan advancing slowly: limited staff and money, weak monitoring and little involvement of the environment sector.

sources.title: Establishing antimicrobial resistance surveillance & research network in India: journey so far
sources.takeaway: Describes how a national hospital-based AMR surveillance and research network was built and what it showed: rising resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, so data must drive action.

sources.title: Containment of a country-wide outbreak of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Israeli hospitals via a nationally implemented intervention
sources.takeaway: A coordinated national programme with strict isolation rules, reporting and oversight stopped an outbreak that individual hospitals had not been able to contain.

sources.title: Effectiveness of national and subnational infection prevention and control interventions in high-income and upper-middle-income countries: a systematic review
sources.takeaway: Across 29 studies, national infection control programmes generally helped, most clearly multi-part approaches and surveillance with feedback.

sources.title: The pursuit of responsible use of medicines: sharing and learning from country experiences
sources.takeaway: WHO compilation of country experiences with policies that improved how medicines are used, including enforcement of prescription-only sales.

sources.title: The next step to further decrease veterinary antibiotic applications: phytogenic alternatives and effective monitoring; the Dutch approach
sources.takeaway: Antibiotic use on Dutch farms fell sharply after national reduction goals but is levelling off; the authors point to alternatives and better monitoring as the next step.

sources.title: One Health in action: operational aspects of an integrated surveillance system for zoonoses in western Kenya
sources.takeaway: A field pilot of integrated zoonoses surveillance showed that engaging local stakeholders and feeding results back quickly keeps participants involved.

sources.title: Prioritizing zoonoses for global health capacity building: themes from One Health zoonotic disease workshops in 7 countries
sources.takeaway: Lessons from seven country workshops that prioritised zoonoses with a One Health approach.
sources.note: Authors not read; record taken from the JEE tool's source list.

sources.title: The effectiveness of biosecurity interventions in reducing the transmission of bacteria from livestock to humans at the farm level: a systematic literature review
sources.takeaway: In 14 studies, farm biosecurity measures may reduce spread of bacteria from animals to people, but good evidence on which measures work best is scarce.

sources.title: Advances in whole genome sequencing for foodborne pathogens: implications for clinical infectious disease surveillance and public health
sources.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
sources.takeaway: Whole genome sequencing traces foodborne outbreak sources in far finer detail than older methods; cost, skills and data sharing remain barriers.

sources.title: Multinational collaboration in solving a European Salmonella Braenderup outbreak linked to imported melons, 2021
sources.takeaway: Cross-border data sharing quickly traced a multi-country Salmonella outbreak to imported melons from Honduras.
sources.note: Journal name inferred from the file name on the repository record.

sources.title: Interventions for improving coverage of childhood immunisation in low- and middle-income countries
sources.takeaway: Strategies such as health education, home-based records and involving community leaders may raise vaccination coverage, though certainty of evidence is mostly low.

sources.title: Feasibility and acceptability of oral cholera vaccine mass vaccination campaign in response to an outbreak and floods in Malawi
sources.takeaway: A reactive cholera vaccination campaign after floods in Nsanje reached most of its target group, was well accepted and caused no serious adverse events.

sources.title: Systematic approach towards establishing a National Inventory of Dangerous Pathogens
sources.takeaway: Step-by-step method to set up and maintain a national record of facilities that hold dangerous pathogens; it also shows where collections can be consolidated.

sources.title: Establishment of a National Inventory of Dangerous Pathogens in the Republic of Uganda
sources.takeaway: Country example of building a national pathogen inventory in a low-resource setting, including the facility survey.
sources.note: Supplied by Mark van Passel; authors as listed by the RIVM WHO Collaborating Centre.

sources.title: Development of a biosecurity checklist for laboratory assessment and monitoring
sources.takeaway: A checklist to assess and monitor laboratory biosecurity, usable for audits.

sources.title: The Vulnerability Scan, a web tool to increase institutional biosecurity resilience
sources.takeaway: A free web-based self-assessment of an institution's biosecurity vulnerabilities.

sources.title: Laboratory-acquired infections in Canada, 2016 to 2021
sources.takeaway: National analysis of laboratory-acquired infections reported to Canada's mandatory reporting system, useful as a model for learning from incidents.

sources.title: Uganda's new national laboratory sample transport system: a successful model for improving access to diagnostic services for early infant HIV diagnosis and other programs
sources.takeaway: A courier network linking regional hubs to 616 facilities cut delays and transport costs for infant HIV tests and widened access.

sources.title: Evidence from 617 laboratories in 47 countries for SLMTA-driven improvement in quality management systems
sources.takeaway: Audit scores in 617 laboratories rose substantially after SLMTA training, suggesting lasting quality improvement in low-resource laboratories.

sources.title: From grass to grace: how SLMTA revolutionised the Bamenda Regional Hospital Laboratory in Cameroon
sources.takeaway: A hospital laboratory went from lowest to highest score in the quality programme through training, on-site mentoring and team effort.

sources.title: The laboratory health system and its response to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in Liberia
sources.takeaway: A fragmented laboratory system with no local testing for dangerous fevers slowed the Ebola response; rebuilding capacity, training and accreditation are the lessons.

sources.title: Event-based surveillance at health facility and community level in low-income and middle-income countries: a systematic review
sources.takeaway: In 13 systems reviewed, facility and community event-based surveillance strengthened early warning, especially when linked to existing response structures.

sources.title: Evaluation of national event-based surveillance, Nigeria, 2016–2018
sources.takeaway: The system picked up real outbreaks well, but weak logging and the lack of written procedures limited oversight and follow-up.
sources.note: First author as shown on the EID page.

sources.title: Twenty years of integrated disease surveillance and response in Sub-Saharan Africa: challenges and opportunities for effective management of infectious disease epidemics
sources.takeaway: IDSR is still mostly facility- and indicator-based; broader data sources and multisector platforms are needed to use surveillance data better.

sources.title: Public health workforce capacities and the challenges for preparedness
sources.takeaway: Scoping review: many countries have no dedicated public health workforce policy or plan, so defining and monitoring the workforce is a first step for preparedness.
sources.note: Authors not listed on the page read.

sources.title: The link between the West African Ebola outbreak and health systems in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone: a systematic review
sources.takeaway: Health-worker shortages hampered Ebola control and were themselves made worse by the outbreak, so staffing and basic health-system capacity need strengthening.

sources.title: Evaluation of field epidemiology training programs: a scoping review
sources.takeaway: Across 12 evaluations, field epidemiology training seems to build trainee skills in several formats, but standard metrics and better evaluation tools are needed.

sources.title: Emergency medical teams in WHO's Western Pacific Region
sources.takeaway: Emergency medical teams now exist in almost all Western Pacific countries; steady funding, cooperation and research are needed to keep them effective.

sources.title: What do 32 COVID-19 deployments of emergency medical teams tell us about challenges and lessons learned?
sources.journal: Report from the Field, Cambridge University Press (Society for Disaster Medicine and Public Health)
sources.takeaway: Deployments called for large, flexible staff rosters, better needs assessments and closer coordination with health ministries.

sources.title: Dynamic preparedness metric: a paradigm shift to measure and act on preparedness
sources.authors: Kandel N, Chungong S, et al.
sources.takeaway: An approach for measuring readiness regularly and acting on the gaps found.

sources.title: Sustainable model for public health emergency operations centers for global settings
sources.takeaway: Lessons from building emergency operations centres in several countries, distilled into a sustainable model.

sources.title: Ebola virus disease outbreak — Nigeria, July–September 2014
sources.takeaway: An emergency operations centre using an incident management system coordinated the response and helped contain Ebola early.

sources.title: Investing in national public health institutes for future pandemics: lessons from Nigeria
sources.takeaway: How Nigeria built its national public health institute and a network of emergency operations centres.

sources.title: An overview of national approaches to stockpiling of medical countermeasures for public health emergencies
sources.takeaway: Compares how countries organise stockpiles and supplier agreements for medical countermeasures.

sources.title: Building research capacity in low- and middle-income countries and pandemic preparedness: lessons learned and future directions
sources.journal: American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
sources.takeaway: Local research capacity (trained staff, genomic sequencing, partnerships) is essential for responding to pandemics in low- and middle-income countries.

sources.title: Strengthening health disaster risk management in Africa: multi-sectoral and people-centred approaches are required in the post-Hyogo Framework of Action era
sources.takeaway: The regional health disaster strategy fell behind its targets, mainly through weak political commitment and funding; the authors call for multisectoral, people-centred approaches.

sources.title: Hospital safety index: assessing the readiness and resiliency of hospitals in Indonesia
sources.takeaway: In 15 hospitals the average Hospital Safety Index grade suggested emergency functioning could be at risk, so short-term fixes were needed.

sources.title: Hospital safety index: evaluation of the readiness and safety of hospitals in Isfahan province, Iran
sources.takeaway: The 55 hospitals became safer between 2017 and 2022 on the WHO Hospital Safety Index, but disaster readiness still has room to improve.

sources.title: Key lessons learnt from COVID-19 intra-action reviews in the Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, Kosovo and North Macedonia 2020–2021: a qualitative study
sources.takeaway: Across four reviews staff shortages were a key barrier, and learning together across sectors strengthened preparedness.

sources.title: First COVID-19 intra-action review: experience from Kenya
sources.takeaway: Kenya's 2021 review found good practices but also funding, data and supply gaps; regular reviews can strengthen future preparedness.

sources.title: WHO SPH portal record: partnership to link public health and security authorities in Cambodia (US Indo-Pacific Command, FAO, WHO)
sources.authors: WHO Strategic Partnership for Health Security
sources.takeaway: A partnership supports Cambodia, with FAO and WHO as implementers, to connect public health and security authorities when a deliberate biological event is suspected.

sources.title: Community Care Centre (CCC) as adjunct in the management of Ebola virus disease (EVD) cases during outbreaks: experience from Sierra Leone
sources.takeaway: Community care centres helped sick people isolate and get care near home, but exposed uninfected patients to risk and lacked staff support.

sources.title: Maintaining essential health services during COVID-19: cross-country lessons of health system resilience from Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America
sources.takeaway: Strong primary care, earlier epidemic experience and public trust helped keep essential services running.

sources.title: Assessing capacities and resilience of health services during the COVID-19 pandemic: lessons from rapid key informant surveys
sources.takeaway: Experience with rapid surveys to monitor service disruptions during the pandemic.
sources.note: Authors not read; record taken from the JEE tool's source list.

sources.title: Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on utilisation of healthcare services: a systematic review
sources.takeaway: Use of health services fell by about a third in the first months of the pandemic, more so for milder conditions.

sources.title: Core components for effective infection prevention and control programmes: new WHO evidence-based recommendations
sources.takeaway: The WHO guideline sets out eleven recommendations on what national and facility IPC programmes need to be effective.

sources.title: Surveillance of healthcare-associated bloodstream and urinary tract infections in a national level network of Indian hospitals
sources.takeaway: A network of 37 hospitals tracked bloodstream and urinary infections with adapted protocols and found high drug resistance and two outbreaks.

sources.title: Environmental conditions in health care facilities in low- and middle-income countries: coverage and inequalities
sources.journal: International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health
sources.takeaway: Only about 2% of health facilities had water, sanitation, hygiene and waste services all in place.
sources.note: Link goes to the university's news item on the study.

sources.title: Integrating emergency risk communication (ERC) into the public health system response: systematic review of literature to aid formulation of the 2017 WHO guideline
sources.takeaway: The evidence behind the WHO guideline on integrating risk communication into emergency response.

sources.title: Social mobilization and community engagement central to the Ebola response in West Africa: lessons for future public health emergencies
sources.takeaway: Trusted local messengers, flexible but coordinated communication and sustained community involvement were central to the response.

sources.title: The importance of community health workers as frontline responders during the COVID-19 pandemic, Somalia, 2020–2021
sources.takeaway: Community health workers found about a third of suspected cases and traced more contacts than facilities did, which helps in hard-to-reach areas.

sources.title: Infodemic management using digital information and knowledge cocreation to address COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy: case study from Ghana
sources.takeaway: Ghana built a weekly, human-verified social listening workflow to spot and answer COVID-19 vaccine misinformation in near real time.

sources.title: WHO competency framework for health authorities and institutions to manage infodemics
sources.takeaway: Competencies and roles needed in staff who manage infodemics.
sources.note: Authors not read; record taken from the JEE tool's source list.

sources.title: Assessing core capacities for addressing public health emergencies of international concern at designated points of entry in Cameroon during the COVID-19 pandemic
sources.takeaway: All five designated points of entry fell short of standards, mainly through unstructured communication, missing emergency plans and too few trained staff.

sources.title: Exit and entry screening practices for infectious diseases among travelers at points of entry: looking for evidence on public health impact
sources.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 16(23)
sources.takeaway: Border screening rarely caught infected travellers but may raise awareness; it works best combined with other outbreak measures.

sources.title: Travel-related control measures to contain the COVID-19 pandemic: a rapid review
sources.takeaway: Rapid review of travel measures for COVID-19 using observational and modelling studies, with SARS and MERS as indirect evidence; see the review for effect estimates.
sources.note: Authors and year are from memory of the Cochrane record; the page read did not show them. Results not read.

sources.title: Ranking the effectiveness of worldwide COVID-19 government interventions
sources.takeaway: No single measure pushed the reproduction number below one; well-timed combinations worked best, with limits on gatherings and school closures among the most effective.

sources.title: Responding to chemical events: a multisectoral responsibility
sources.takeaway: Report of a regional consultation: chemical emergencies need a multisectoral response and health ministries must ensure coordinated national capacity, which many countries lack.

sources.title: Lessons learned from radiation protection for emergency response and remediation/decontamination work relating to the Fukushima accident
sources.journal: Journal of the National Institute of Public Health 67(1)
sources.takeaway: Narrative review of 2012–2017 papers: worker radiation protection is rarely reported, and lessons should shape preparedness for future nuclear accidents.
sources.note: Title as abbreviated on the journal page.
